title: Open Water
description: You're Top Gun, living high in the sky, and got a need for speed. When suddenly, you find yourself in the danger zone, what do you do? You eject, surviving the perils above only to face the terrors below, alone, out at sea. Spc. Stephen Solomon reports training lead by survival evasion resistance and escape, or sere, experts. No matter the terrain, it's always important to take the time to train your body, mind, and spirit what it takes to survive. Soundbites from SSSGT Nick Weber, LTC Colleen Kelly.
keywords: top gun, trainee, water survival, Stephen Solomon, Colleen Kelly, Nick Weber, aviation, sea

transcript.text: - [Voiceover] At the Outdoor Rec swimming pool,
a couple of experts in SERE were training personnel.
- [Voiceover] Basically, everything
that they would need to know in that situation.
- [Voiceover] That situation being:
What would they do if they had to eject
and parachute into the sea?
- And then, once they land in the water,
we go over what to do
if they find themselves under the canopy.
They actually had to go under the canopy,
hand-over-hand, (splashing)
and make it to the other side, without freaking out
which they all did a good job.
So then, from there, what we did is we actually had them
practice the different drags,
both on their stomach an on their back,
exactly what to do in case that parachute inflates with air
and they're getting drug across the ocean.
And, once again, everybody did that successfully,
no hiccups there.
The last part to it was Open Ocean Survival,
so we had everybody get in a one-man life raft
and experience what it would be like
to be in that situation,
how to take care of their basic needs
as well as understand everything in their survival kit.
- [Voiceover] And, reflecting back,
how did the participants in the training
respond to their instructions?
- There's a degree of enthusiasm and respect and just a joy
and, just really, that they get into it.
What can I say (laughs)?
And, on top of it, the training was excellent.
Everybody really, really, really does a great job
and I'm quite privileged to be able to be here.
I'm glad to be here to help out,
but having a fantastic time, while here.
- [Voiceover] I'm Specialist Stephen Solomon,
(splashing) Pusan Air Base, Korea.

pass_reason: training drill presented as training, no real rescue or outcome
